title: Make Array Alternate in Parity
statement:
You are given an array `nums` of `n` positive integers. In one operation you may pick any index `i` and replace `nums[i]` with `floor(nums[i] / 2)`. You may apply the operation to the same element as many times as you like, so an element can become `0` (and `0` counts as an even number).

The array must end up **alternating in parity**, following one of these two patterns:

- `Odd, Even, Odd, Even, ...`
- `Even, Odd, Even, Odd, ...`

Return the **minimum number of operations** needed to make the array follow either pattern. If the array already alternates, the answer is `0`.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` integers `nums[0] ... nums[n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the minimum number of operations.

examples.explanation: For `Odd, Even, Odd, Even`: 6 becomes 3 with one operation, while 12 (even), 5 (odd) and 10 (even) are already right, so the cost is 1. The other pattern costs 4: 12 -> 6 -> 3 (2 operations), 5 -> 2 (1) and 10 -> 5 (1). The minimum is 1.
The array is already `Odd, Even, Odd, Even`.
For `Odd, Even, Odd`: change the middle 1 into 0 (1 operation). For `Even, Odd, Even` both ends must become 0 (2 operations). The minimum is 1.

hints: Each element can be fixed independently once you decide which pattern the array follows.
For one element and one target parity, simulate halving until the parity matches; this takes at most about 30 steps.
Compute the total cost of both patterns in a single pass and print the smaller one.
